abi.r1: current reading, the candidate RT byte read at 0x1e0cee2
abi.r4: base pointer supplied by the caller; state is addressed as base+index

per_channel_state.+0x7c: armed byte - this is what the return value is derived from

behaviour: current < previous (decreasing): if mode == 0, set mode = 1, clear the armed byte, and set the armed byte only when the drop is at least 0x1f (31).
current < previous with mode != 0: increment the counter; after 3 consecutive decreases clear the armed byte.

current > previous (increasing): if mode == 1, set mode = 0 and clear the armed byte; otherwise increment the counter and, if the rise is at least 0x1e (30) relative to the previous value, clear the armed byte after 5 consecutive increases.
previous is then updated to the current reading and the return value is 0xFF when the armed byte is non-zero, otherwise 0x00.
return_semantics: 0xFF (non-zero) or 0x00 only - never an analogue value
interpretation: A per-channel arming/hysteresis state machine with a large-drop fast path (>= 31 counts) and consecutive-sample counters (3 on the way down, 5 on the way up). It converts a noisy analogue reading into a stable armed/not-armed decision.
what_this_means_for_the_D2_question: The caller writes this 0xFF/0x00 return straight into the candidate RT byte at sp+1093 and sets or clears mask bit 0x200 from the same non-zero test. So the byte the D2 frame carries for RT is NOT the analogue reading when this path runs - it is the armed decision. That is a candidate explanation for the observed 0/17/27/96/255 spread and for why an analogue-only change need not produce the same edge: an intermediate value is only visible when the analogue copy path writes the byte instead.
not_proven: whether the same helper serves LT (the LT byte is set to 0xff directly in the synthesis block, and 0x1e0a426 has only one caller in this image)
the meaning of the mode byte beyond its 0/1 use
the full caller context that supplies r4
evidence: PROVEN STATIC at instruction level; no live validation
